verdicts.reason: Quote states the integrator must supply clock frequency/period and uncertainty before STA. Actor 'system' is acceptable; nothing is checkable in simulation, so check=none.

The quote says no CDC exceptions are required. That is a statement of fact, not a prohibition on a behaviour, so MUST_NOT is wrong. The single-clock-domain claim is a description. The 'apply only justified constraints' part is covered by AA-17.1.3-03. The rule is best treated as a SHOULD_NOT/MAY at most, and it adds nothing verifiable.
The quote is an explicit prohibition on declaring async clock groups or false paths between bridge logic and FIFO pointers. It is a constraint-flow rule, so check=none.

The quote says to apply only justified reset, generated-clock or memory-macro constraints and not to invent numeric exceptions. MUST is acceptable for 'shall apply only'. It is a constraint-flow rule, so check=none.
The quote says the FIFO storage must be mapped to standard cells or a compatible single-clock memory macro. It is a synthesis/implementation requirement, so check=none.

duplicates.reason: Both rules cite the same quote about applying only justified reset, generated-clock or memory-macro constraints with no invented numeric exception. AA-17.1.3-01 restates this and adds a descriptive single-clock claim.

questions.question: AA-17.1.3-01 says no CDC exceptions are required, but AA-17.1.3-03 allows justified reset, generated-clock or memory-macro constraints. Should AA-17.1.3-01 be read as a statement of fact or as a prohibition? Who decides what counts as 'justified'?
